newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Power outage strikes Malaysian capital.
newsitem.headline: Power outage strikes Malaysian capital.

text.p: A power outage struck three key areas of the Malaysian capital's business district on Tuesday afternoon but power authorities expected electricity to resume later in the evening.
Malaysian state power utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd said electricity supply should be restored to Kuala Lumpur's central business area after 8.00 p.m. (1200 GMT).
"We think it'll be back after 8.00 p.m.," a spokeswoman for Tenaga told Reuters.
Power had already been restored to some areas by 1030 GMT, witnesses said.

The power outage follows a massive blackout on peninsular Malaysia in August this year which lasted between 12 to 15 hours and caused major embarrassment for the country. That outage resulted in the replacement of Tenaga's executive chairman.
A Tenaga spokesman earlier said three main areas in the capital's business district, Jalan Sultan Ismail, Jalan Raja Chulan and Jalan Bukit Bintang, were suffering from lost power.
"We've got many calls from affected consumers in Jalan Sultan Ismail, Jalan Raja Chulan and Jalan Bukit Bintang," the spokesman said.
